You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Compared with the source, has the image been transformed into a coherent chalk drawing, with drawing-like rendering replacing substantial photographic structure in both the subjects and the background?
node.criteria: Pass only when the main subjects and surrounding scene are rendered as a coherent chalk-made drawing: drawing-like forms and chalk marks replace substantial source-like photographic anatomy, patterns, and scene detail in both subjects and background. Fail when there is no meaningful chalk-drawing treatment, or when chalk-like grain, softened outlines, smudging, or shading is visible but substantial photographic structure or detail remains in either the subjects or background. Texture, scene-wide coverage, or recognizable chalk effects alone do not establish completion. Unknown if the source or edited image is unavailable or evidence is insufficient to judge.
node.binding: Compare the source and edited images. Explicitly assess residual source-like photographic structure separately in the subjects and the background, as well as whether drawing-like forms and chalk rendering replace it. Do not infer completion from texture or coverage alone. Judge the requested chalk-medium transformation, not a particular style.

node_traces.evidence: Compared with the source, the edited image has a chalk-like grain, softened outlines, and smudged shading. However, both giraffes retain substantial photographic structure, including recognizable anatomy and detailed coat patterns. The background is blurred and chalk-textured, but still preserves source-like scene elements and photographic structure rather than replacing them with clearly drawing-made forms.
